text:
Match each item in Column A with its description in Column B.
Column A
(1) a static method
(2) a method
(3) the return statement
(4) a constructor
Column B
(a) A special member that has the class’s name and runs when an object is made.
(b) The statement that ends a method and sends back a value, if any.
(c) A named block of code in a class, that does one job.
(d) A method that belongs to its class, and is called without an object.

text:
Match each item in Column A with its description in Column B.
Column A
(1) a method body
(2) call by value
(3) method overloading
(4) an instance method
Column B
(a) Several methods with one name, but different parameter lists.
(b) The block of statements that a method runs.
(c) A method that belongs to an object, and can use its fields.
(d) Passing a copy of a value, so that the method can’t change the caller’s variable.

text:
Match each item in Column A with its description in Column B.
Column A
(1) a parameter
(2) a side effect
(3) an argument
(4) a recursive method
Column B
(a) A value passed to a method when it is called.
(b) A variable in a method’s definition, that gets a value when it’s called.
(c) A method that calls itself.
(d) A change a method makes beyond giving back a value, such as altering a field or printing.

text:
Design a class Interest to work out simple interest at 5% a year.
Data members: principal, years.
Member functions:
Interest(double p, int y): a parameterised constructor.
double simple(): returns the simple interest.
void show(): prints the interest.
Specify the class, and define main() to create an object and use it.

points.text: simple() uses the formula, and returns a double.
show() prints the result, calling simple().
main() creates an object, and calls show().
